answer: An umber ledger of earned trust resists Sybil attacks by making identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify. Each newcomer starts on a narrow ledge: a small, verifiable task whose proof is published and linked to a single persistent key. Only after peers confirm that work does the identity earn a violet mark, a time-stamped bloom that deepens with each honest contribution. Splitting into copies means splitting the work: every ledge must be climbed separately, and identities sharing the same key trail are merged and stripped of their marks. Sybil copies stay trapped on the ledge.
